question: Should the department standardise on Protocol A or Protocol B for the next intake cycle?

items.claim: Protocol A cut median turnaround by 19% across four sites (2024-2025 audit, n=1,840).
Protocol A's error rate was non-inferior to B at the pre-registered margin.
Staff training time for A is one day shorter per cohort.
Protocol A is already in use at two partner sites, so transfers need no retraining.
Protocol B has a lower consumable cost per case at current volumes.
Protocol B's escalation pathway is better documented for the night shift.
Protocol B had fewer reported near-misses in the last two quarters.
Protocol A eliminated adverse events entirely in the pilot.
items.source: pilot memo 2024-11 -- RETRACTED 2025-01, denominator error, see erratum

items.claim: An unpublished multi-site trial shows A dominates B on every endpoint.
Protocol B is being withdrawn by its vendor next year.
items.source: rumour reported at 2025-09 standup, vendor denies

notes: status is the evidence-review verdict. 'supported' items have a located, current source. 'retracted' and 'unverified' items did not clear review.
